response:
Diagnosis after eight generations: the archive has a clear new frontier. Conjunctive_CashYield_HardCashCoverage — cash yield multiplied by cash net of maturing debt scaled by total claims — is the best signal on every dimension at once (FMB 5.88, FF5 alpha +7.4% with t = 4.75, Sharpe 0.532) and it does so at the *highest* coverage in the family (0.141), because it needs no act/lct data. That is a substantive economic finding, not a statistical accident: the discriminator between healthy cheap and trap cheap is hard, unencumbered cash relative to the entire claim stack, not net working capital whose receivables and inventory are worth little in a workout. Two design results also now replicate: worst-case conditioning and smoothing each raise alpha reliability, while industry-norming, accrual growth and solvency volatility all destroy the signal. The final consolidation therefore stress-tests the hard-cash channel along the four dimensions that remain economically open — resilience conditioning, which debt to net out, the scaling denominator, and whether hard liquidity and total-claim coverage are complements — plus one dynamic cash-burn test.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_WorstHardCash
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lt), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm is safe only if it has held cash in excess of maturing debt relative to total claims at every point in the recent past; a firm whose current cash position is a one-off, perhaps financed by an asset sale or an equity raise, is still a trap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Worst-case conditioning raised alpha reliability when applied to the net-working-capital buffer, and applying it to the stronger hard-cash channel is the single most likely way to improve on the archive leader. A three-year window is used so the coverage advantage of the cash-based channel is largely preserved.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_TotalDebtNetCash
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: What protects a cheap firm's equity is cash net of all interest-bearing debt, not merely the tranche maturing this year, because long-term debt covenants and eventual refinancing exert pressure well before maturity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates exactly one economic choice against the leader — which debt is netted against cash — and thereby tells us whether the mechanism is near-term refinancing pressure or total debt overhang. Both variants keep total liabilities as the scaling denominator, so the comparison is clean.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_HardCash_AssetScaled
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: If the safety signal is the share of the balance sheet held in unencumbered cash, asset scaling should work as well as claim scaling; if creditor pressure is what matters, dividing by total liabilities is essential.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: When this denominator test was run on the working-capital channel the asset-scaled version held up (alpha +6.1%, t = 4.08), so repeating it on the stronger hard-cash channel resolves whether the family's normalization is about creditor claims or balance-sheet composition. Asset scaling also removes the instability of dividing by very small liability balances, which should tighten the extreme deciles.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_HardCash_And_ClaimCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Hard cash against maturing debt and total current assets against all claims measure different survival resources — immediate settlement capacity versus overall liquidation coverage — so a cheap firm strong on both is the most reliably healthy, and weakness on either is disqualifying.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The earlier three-way conjunction diluted performance, but its third leg was claims turnover, the weakest of the solvency channels, whereas here both solvency legs individually produced 6%-plus alphas. This is the decisive test of whether the two best distress channels are complements or substitutes, which determines the form of the final consolidated signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Conjunctive_SmoothedYield_HardCash
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 3)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable cash-generating capacity measured over three years, interacted with unencumbered cash against total claims, should be the most economically coherent statement of the healthy-cheap concept: sustained cash generation plus settlement capacity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Smoothing the valuation leg raised the alpha t-stat when paired with the working-capital buffer, so pairing it with the superior hard-cash leg tests whether the two best-performing modifications to opposite arguments of the product compound. It also reduces annual rebalancing noise in the long leg, the diagnostic that has tracked Sharpe throughout this family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_CashBurn_Adjusted
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lt), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lt), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Both the level of unencumbered cash and its direction of travel matter: a cheap firm with a modest but growing net cash position is repairing itself, while one with a comparable but rapidly burning position is on a path to the very distress its price implies.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Change-based distress channels have failed twice in this archive, but both attempts used working-capital or leverage accounting aggregates rather than the cash channel that has now proved to be the active ingredient, so a burn-rate test on the right variable is a genuinely new question rather than a repeat. Combining level and change additively inside the solvency leg preserves the multiplicative interaction with cheapness that has been essential throughout.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
